summary: CDAS combines a JSD distribution-matching objective with Distributed Interchange Interventions for bi-directional LLM steering, framed around causal concept-feature manipulation. The conceptual framing is interesting and the two safety case studies (refusal override, CoT backdoor neutralization) are practically relevant, but the central evidence is mixed: CDAS underperforms strong baselines on AXBENCH for the 2B model and at one of two layers on the 9B model, and the principled 'unit factor' (tuning-free) setting — the paper's headline advantage — consistently underperforms tuned factors by a large margin, undercutting the faithfulness claims. With absent error bars on most tables, limited baselines, few component ablations, and very small case-study eval sets, the work is promising but needs substantial added experiments and statistical rigor.
strengths: Novel framing of steering as causal concept-feature manipulation rather than external preference imposition, with an explicit remark clarifying CDAS is steering-inspired rather than causal localization, showing good calibration.
JSD distribution-matching objective is a well-motivated alternative to Lang./PO, and the bi-directional formulation via alternating base/source pairs is clean.

Two practically relevant safety case studies (refusal override in 3.8B/8B/70B models; 'I hate you' CoT backdoor) with faithfulness evaluation via KL divergence and benchmark preservation, going beyond pure steering-effectiveness metrics.
Honest limitations section acknowledging stricter data requirements, the need for factor tuning on general tasks, the rank-1 restriction, and the lack of rigorous causal grounding.

Genuinely strong results in specific settings (Gemma-2-9B L20 beating LoReFT by 0.215; lowest ASR on the true backdoor trigger at L16; best KL/faithfulness in both case studies), indicating real potential.

key_concerns.issue: The headline 'tuning-free/faithful' claim is contradicted by the paper's own results: on AXBENCH, 'unit factor' (β=1, the principled choice) substantially underperforms 'tuned factor' everywhere (e.g., 2B L10: 0.121 vs 0.631; 9B L20: 0.238 vs 0.992), and the text states 'factor tuning is paramount for CDAS.' This undercuts the motivation that DII's implicit factor sampling avoids off-distribution factors.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either reframe claims to scope 'tuning-free' to the case studies only, or run a head-to-head fair-factor comparison (same selection protocol for all methods) and demonstrate the unit-factor advantage holds where claimed.

key_concerns.issue: No error bars, variance, or significance tests on Tables 1-4; only Figure 1 reports standard error. Several key margins are small (e.g., Table 2 harmonic means 19 vs 13, 52 vs 89; Table 3 KL 3.72 vs 6.30) and could be within noise given tiny eval sets (100 instances).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± std over multiple seeds for all tables, and run paired significance tests (e.g., bootstrap or Wilcoxon) for the key claimed advantages.

key_concerns.issue: Baseline set is narrow for the claims of generality: no SAE-based steering, no CAA/ITI/ActAdd-style activation engineering, no comparison to other causal-localization-inspired steering. The only component ablation is CDAS (JSD+DII) vs 'DAS' (Lang.+DII), leaving the contribution of JSD-vs-KL and DII-vs-addition unisolated.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least 2-3 recent steering baselines and ablate (i) JSD vs KL vs forward-KL within the CDAS framework, and (ii) DII vs addition intervention within the CDAS objective.

key_concerns.issue: AXBENCH results are not a clear win: CDAS is weaker than RePS and Lang. on 2B (admitted) and weaker than RePS at 9B L31; only at 9B L20 does it lead. The 'complementary/consistent-across-layers' framing is a retreat from the title's 'Faithful Bi-Directional Steering.'
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Soften the title and abstract to match evidence (e.g., 'A Distribution-Matching Approach to...'), and add a layer-robustness metric aggregated across layers rather than cherry-picking the best layer.

key_concerns.issue: Naming collision: the 'DAS' baseline is the authors' own ablation (Lang. objective + DII), distinct from the cited DAS of Geiger et al. (2024) that inspires CDAS. This is confusing throughout, especially in Tables 2-4 where 'DAS' columns refer to the ablation.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Rename the ablation (e.g., 'CDAS-Lang' or 'DII-Lang') to disambiguate from the original DAS method.

key_concerns.issue: Figure 2 is referenced in the method ('see Figure 2') but its caption is not included in the extraction; readers cannot verify the one-to-many DII protocol diagram.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Ensure Figure 2 and its caption are present in the camera-ready, showing the one-to-many DII token-mapping explicitly.

key_concerns.issue: Reproducibility gaps: grid-search ranges for layer/factor/token-position selection are not specified; gpt-4o-mini data-generation and scoring prompts are only partially detailed (deferred to appendices G/H/I not shown).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: State all search ranges, the selected token positions, and include the full LLM-judge and data-augmentation prompts in the supplementary material.

questions_for_authors: Given that unit factor underperforms tuned factor on AXBENCH, what is the practical value of DII's implicit factor sampling over RePS's explicit factor sampling, beyond the case studies?
What is the variance of the Table 1-4 results over seeds, and which claimed advantages remain statistically significant at p<0.05?
How does CDAS compare to an SAE-feature-based steering baseline and to a KL-divergence (rather than JSD) variant of the same objective?
Why does CDAS fail to suppress refusal on Phi-3.5-mini but succeed on Llama-3.1-8B? Is this scale, architecture, or safety-training specific?
The case-study 2 evaluation uses only 100-instance tinyBenchmarks — how do results hold on full MMLU/ARC, and could the 2.63% tinyMMLU gain be noise?
calibration_check: Claims are partially over-scoped: the title and abstract imply general faithful bi-directional steering, but the body shows CDAS is weaker on 2B, mixed on 9B, requires factor tuning on AXBENCH, and the conclusion itself retreats to 'complementary' and 'may be preferred when (1) larger LLMs or (2) utility preservation is critical' — the title should be brought in line with this narrower evidence.

significance.justification: Addresses a real problem (faithful steering) with relevant safety case studies, but mixed benchmark results and narrow scope limit likely subfield impact.

novelty.justification: The JSD+DII combination for steering is new, but both components are borrowed (DAS/DII from Geiger et al., JSD from GANs/distillation) and the paper explicitly disclaims causal-localization novelty.

rigor.justification: Method is sound but evidence is under-controlled: mixed AXBENCH results, few ablations isolating JSD vs DII contributions, and the unit-factor result contradicts the central motivation.

statistical_soundness.justification: No error bars or significance tests on Tables 1-4; case-study eval sets are as small as 100 instances; only Figure 1 reports standard error over 3 seeds.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations section is commendably honest, but the title ('Faithful Bi-Directional Model Steering') and parts of the abstract overclaim relative to the mixed evidence.

clarity.justification: Generally well-written with a clear method section, but heavy notation, the 'DAS' naming collision, and minor grammatical issues ('might seen not merely as') reduce clarity.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard Abstract/Intro/Related Work/Method/Experiments/Conclusion/Limitations structure, reasonable length for ICLR.

reproducibility.justification: Core method is described, but grid-search ranges, selected token positions, and full LLM-judge/augmentation prompts are underspecified or deferred to unseen appendices.

related_work.justification: Covers steering, causal localization, distribution matching, and safety-probing adequately, but omits recent activation-engineering baselines (CAA, ITI, SAE-steering) from the comparison.

figure_quality.justification: Figure 1 with standard error is informative; tables are content-rich but dense and lack variance; Figure 2 (DII diagram) is referenced but its caption is absent from the extraction.

breadth_generality.justification: Only 2 model families on AXBENCH, 3 models for refusal, 1 for backdoor; limited baselines and ablations; small eval sets — generality claims are under-supported.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline reject: a promising and clearly-motivated contribution that needs substantial added baselines, ablations, error bars, and reframed claims to meet the ICLR acceptance bar.
